predecessors.name: Uruk
predecessors.text: Sumer: Utu-hengal's kingdom, taken by his 'governor of Ur, Ur-Nammu'

predecessors.name: Second Dynasty of Lagash
predecessors.text: Lagash: 'He slew Nam-ha-ni the ensi of Lagash' (Code of Ur-Nammu)

predecessors.name: Elam
predecessors.text: Akkad, Eshnunna and Akshak, which Kutik-Inshushinak had taken, 'reconquered' by Ur-Nammu, then Susa, 'overrun by the Third dynasty of Ur under Ur-Nammu and his son Shulgi'

successors.name: Isin
successors.text: Isin and Nippur under Ishbi-Erra, who 'formed an independent kingdom' c.

successors.name: Elam
successors.text: Ur, sacked and held 'through military occupation for the next 21 years', and Susa

ledger.x: 2112 BCE: Ur-Nammu founds the Third Dynasty of Ur.

2049 BCE: Shulgi's year 45: he 'smashed the heads of Urbilum, Simurrum, Lullubum and Karhar in a single campaign'; Simurrum and Lullubum were destroyed nine times 'between the 26th and 45th years of his reign', Der in year 21, Karhar in 24 and 31, Harshi in 27, Kimash and Hurti in 45–46.
ledger.cp: Zagros highland polities (Simurrum, Lullubum, Urbilum, Karhar)

ledger.x: 2025 BCE: Naplanum rules Larsa inside the realm.
2024 BCE: Lagash stops dating by Ur.

ledger.cp: Zagros highland polities (Simurrum, Lullubum, Urbilum, Karhar)

ledger.x: 2004 BCE: Larsa's dynasty outlives its suzerain.
2004 BCE: Ur falls to the Elamites and Shimashki.

wars.name: Shulgi's Zagros and Elamite campaigns
wars.outcome: Year names: Der destroyed (21), Karhar (24, 31), Simurrum (25, 27, 32, nine times to 44), Harshi (27), Anshan (34, after the governor of Anshan married the king's daughter in 30), the wall of the land built (37) against 'the Tidnumite nomads', Shashrum (42)…

wars.name: Shu-Sin's campaign against Zabshali and Shimashki
wars.outcome: 'Year Shu-Sin, the king of Ur, king of the four quarters, destroyed the land of Zabshali' (his sixth year); authority asserted in Shimanum, Zabshali and Shimashki; 'a new wall' built against the Amorites.

wars.name: Fall of Ur
wars.outcome: The provinces fell away to Isin and the Amorites; the Elamite and Shimashki army under Kindattu sacked Ur c.

certainty.note: The core is a dated administrative record ('about twenty provinces', year names, the bala) but no boundary survey; the periphery 'from Urbilum to Pashime and Susa' is a tribute belt with garrisons and is drawn soft; 'the wall of the land'…
